Introduction.question:
Hallo. Thank you for making time for us today.

I work with CIMMYT, an organization that conducts research to improve the production of maize, wheat, and other crops in different countries across Africa, Asia, and Latin America.

We are carrying out this study to learn about farmers’ experiences, challenges, and preferences when growing white maize. The information you share will help researchers better understand farmers’ needs and support the development of better maize varieties in the future.

During the interview, we will use a mobile phone to help record and organize your responses. This will help us capture your answers accurately and make sure we do not miss any important information.

Your participation is voluntary. You may choose not to answer any question or stop the interview at any time. The information you provide will be kept private and used only for research purposes. There are no right or wrong answers—we simply want to hear about your real experiences and views.

The interview will take about 45 minutes.

Thank you very much for taking part in this study.

The study is led by Dr. Mercy Mbugua. If you have any questions or concerns about the study, you can contact her on +254 724 740 197.

If you have any concerns or questions, you can reach her by mobile: +254 724 740 197.

Q13.answer:

Q14.question: If you use white maize to feed livestock, which animals do you feed it to and how often?
Q14.answer:
May stop, or the Mays, we feed down poultry and sometimes we grind it and we transform them to maize jam.
 Since we don't have so much production, maize jam we buy directly and it is an everyday thing.
 Since on the side of the dairy cattle we feed maize jam together with dairy milk so we feed them dairy.
 Also on poultry we grind them and mix with other concentrates.
 On that one we improve the nutrition of the poultry.
 So in season we find that the poultry is ground maize and as well as other maize concentrates so it is continuous.
 So I think it is daily basis.

Q15.question: Where do you usually obtain the white maize seed that you plant, and why do you prefer getting it there?
Q15.answer:
We mostly get them from either the agrobrates or some things under the co-parity, the milk
 co-parity, we bring us the milk seeds.
 The reason why I prefer getting those seeds is because they are the first generation of
 I-phones.
 And like probably if I repeat the same seeds that I had done in the previous season for
 the yielding will not be as equal as the fast-forwarding.
 So that is the reason why I use them and those are the sources.

Q16.question: Where do you usually sell your maize after harvest, and why do you prefer selling there or to that buyer?
Q16.answer:
Mostly, they sell in the local market as well as in the formal markets.
 For formal markets, at least they have a taste of the maize that I produce.
 So throughout, do you want the green maize?
 And tell me, we want this number of maize.
 The prices are premium.
 So that is one of the reasons why I sell to formal markets.
 Their prices are premium.
 And at least there's not so much negation.
 So, that's another reason why I sell to formal markets.
 Secondly, the question is, for grid 1, I sell to markets, grid 2,
 compared to the local market.
 Another grid 3 is what I can keep for the animals.

Q7.question: Has fall armyworm ever affected your maize? If yes, what damage or losses did it cause?
Q7.answer:
And the damage can't be quantified really, but for whatever happens is if the plants are well fed,
 they'll have some kind of retardation at first or start the growth, then they'll get still to the point of maturing.
 So you'll be able to harvest some ease, but not as good as to the wind without the effect of the falla-livum,
 as well as even the falla itself is partially affected.
 Since on the sides of the leaves and stuff, you'll be able to harvest enough falla as you would have harvested without the effect of the falla.

Q8.question: If you could harvest your maize 20 days earlier but this reduced your yield, how much yield would you be willing to lose to harvest earlier?
Q8.answer: So if I can wait for the 20 days, then half the full production, that will be better.

Q9.question: What level of pest or disease damage would make you switch to a different maize variety?
Q9.answer:
So no matter how little the loss is and there's a better variety, I'll go for the next one.
 When if I am losing 10% and there's a better variety, I'll switch to a better variety.

Q10.question: What specific yield increase would make you consider planting a new maize variety?
Q10.answer:
In my case, I harvest green maize. Green maize makes better returns for me.
 So, maybe the size of the comb, if I have a lot of it, I will sell it.
 Because that one will still give you a fetch in the market also.
 You see, like for maize, it will go and sell.
 If the grass is bigger, it looks more fresh and green.
 When the rest are selling their yards, maybe at 20 shillings, mine I can sell at 25 shillings because of the size.
 Still, I have to consider also, because I'm a farmer and I keep dairy cattle.
 If still the size of the crop, of the folder itself, the maize stalks.
 If it is bigger than the previous ones, you see, like there are those varieties of maize we are buying.
 You find that it's yielding very big maize, but has very little folder.
 Even a kid can go and harvest.
 That one is ideal for a person who is selling on maize.
 But for me, who is also doing the folder side, I want big stalk, big maize, green maize.
 So, that one, I bet.
 If the two, I don't know how I can fresh it in quantities.
 But those are the two things that gives me the choice of the maize that I'm planting.

Q10.question: What specific yield increase would make you consider planting a new maize variety instead of your current one?
Q10.answer:
So for example, you see in a nacre, you might find you are producing maybe 24 dachie bugs.
 So if when you are doing the dry maize, you are able to maybe out of the dachie bugs that you have
 in your mission, the new crop that you are going to plant in your need, be able to harvest even that
 five bugs or 40 bugs. You see when you go to the figures, cannot still change your bugs.
 So even that slight change is ideal for me to make a different choice.

Q11.question: What is the lowest maize yield that would make you continue planting this variety despite a bad season?
Q11.answer:
lower than the years on the missed variety that I had done.
 For example, if the season yes was bad and the rest were harvesting 20 and the missed
 variety harvest maybe 10 or lower than 10 then that variety will be a result sufficient
 for me to switch.

Q7.question: Can you specify the yield loss or crop damage caused by fall armyworm infestation?
Q7.answer:
Around 25% even down from Okipo.
 We give it at 25% since I told you the crop performance tillow was.
 It's not that you won't be able to harvest.
 Mostly if your crops are well fed.
 On the basis of my new application and there was water.
 We will still harvest.
 But the production won't be as equal as if there was no manifestation.

Q9.question: What specific percentage of yield loss would prompt you to switch to a different maize variety?
Q9.answer:
So for me I wouldn't want any loss. So based on that if there is a variety that is
 drought resistant or pest resistant, I will always switch to that because even if it is 5%
 it is still lost when you are trying to curb losses. So I am here to try and maximize production.
 So no matter how little the loss is and there is another option, a better option,
 I go for a better option.
